question: Can I Permanently Delete an Order, and Should I?
metaDescription: Technically yes via the Trash, but it removes accounting and legal records — cancelling or refunding is almost always the better choice.
shortAnswer: Technically yes — moving an order to Trash and then permanently deleting it removes the record entirely. Whether you should is a different question: most jurisdictions have tax and accounting record-keeping requirements that a genuinely completed or refunded transaction needs to satisfy, and permanently deleting a real order can create compliance problems later, even if it seemed harmless at the time. Cancelling (which keeps the record but marks it void) is almost always the better choice over actual deletion.

bodyHtml:
Why This Needs Caution

An order record isn't just a WooCommerce convenience — for any order where money genuinely changed hands, it's also effectively a financial and tax record. Deleting it doesn't just tidy up the admin orders list; it removes evidence of a transaction that may be needed for tax filing, an accounting reconciliation, or a future customer dispute, none of which can be reconstructed once the record is gone.

When Deletion Is Reasonable

  • Genuine test orders placed during development or testing, with no real payment or customer involved, are safe and sensible to delete entirely rather than cluttering real order data.
  • Spam or clearly fraudulent order attempts that never resulted in a real transaction are also reasonable to delete, though even here, keeping them briefly for pattern analysis can be useful before cleanup.
  • A genuine, paid customer order should essentially never be permanently deleted — cancel or refund it instead, preserving the record while accurately reflecting its final status.
  • Bulk cleanup of old abandoned/failed orders (the ones responsible for order-number gaps, covered elsewhere) is sometimes done for database size reasons, but even here, exporting a backup copy first is a sensible precaution.

A Sensible Approach

  1. Reserve permanent deletion for genuine test/spam orders only, never real customer transactions.
  2. Use Cancel or Refund for any real order that needs to be voided, preserving the record.
  3. Export a backup before any bulk cleanup of old abandoned orders, just in case.
  4. Check with an accountant on record-retention requirements for your specific jurisdiction if unsure.
